rules.numbers: every number, date or amount in a post must be one of the item's allowed_numbers or context_numbers, as written there (- and − alike); never the same number twice in a post
rules.picks: never name or hint at the #1 pick; it is locked and not in this file
rules.no_advice: no buy / sell calls, predictions or price targets; every post carries the disclaimer
rules.descriptive: chart_pattern and moves_like describe what happened only (no forecasts; their items' banned_words apply too); moves_like may cashtag only the peers listed in its item
rules.cashtags: at most 4 distinct cashtags, all from the item's tickers + context_tickers; a single-ticker item names its own $TICKER; moves_like may add its peers, picks_ready the public picks
rules.order: items are sorted by audience_rank (rank / rank_why: recognisability, magnitude, freshness, novelty); the first 8 (top8 true) are a varied menu: at most 2 session-map items (P1 P2 P6 P7), at most one small cap, no lead ticker or headline number repeated between them, 4+ pillars when the day has them; items below carry top8_out (why). Pick across pillars per variety

verbatim.rule: VERBATIM FACTS + CLOSED HOOKS (HQ 2026-10-19; round 7 for every item that has phrasings): every sentence of a post, self-reply or comment is EITHER one of the item's phrasings (fact_phrases / claim_phrases; each listed in phrasings with its id) COPIED VERBATIM as its own sentence (only case, spacing, punctuation, $ on cashtags and dash types may differ; a closing '(number)' may be left off; no partial copies, no splicing, no word added, dropped or changed, no 'And' / 'Monday recap:' in front) OR one of the approved hook sentences in hooks, copied WHOLE (its platforms, its item types and its use: post = posts and self-replies, comment = comments on other accounts' posts). There is no free wording at all: no hook made up from words, no comparison outside the phrases, never advice. 'Not investment advice.' stays in every post. A comment without an item_id holds only comment hooks. ROTATION: a phrasing id used in one of the last min(5, k - 1) own posts of the same item type on the same platform is rejected, k = the number of phrasings of its fact (3 phrasings: cycle them); a hook id likewise over the hooks of the item type; drafts already approved count at once, before they are posted; each item's rotation shows the ids used per platform when the file was built, and each phrasing's recent_on the platforms where it is blocked (the validator reads the live post log). Pick a different phrasing of the fact (same numbers, other order) and a different hook every time. Hashtags: only the generic ones listed here (and the item type's topic hashtags); emoji: only hook_emoji. Plain letters only. Use an item of today's facts (usable through the next weekday after its facts date; picks until valid_until); an item from a facts file without fact_phrases is never usable. Links: the item's page_url or source written in full (https://...), never a domain with a path typed bare.

rules.claim_phrases: SUPERSEDED by rules.verbatim for every item with fact_phrases (copy a claim phrase verbatim, as its own sentence). Older items: ALLOWLIST (HQ 2026-10-19): any sentence of a post that compares, ranks or orders anything - best / worst / biggest / largest / most / least / top / led / #N / first / second / next / then / followed by / only / all / every / none / record / ever / since / streak / in a row / again / double / twice / half / N times / more than / less than / any '-er than' / beat / missed / outperformed / lagged / winner / loser / last / bottom, and every other word like them - must be one of the item's claim_phrases, copied verbatim as its own sentence (only 'and' / 'also' / 'so' / 'plus' may stand around it). No claim phrase for what you want to say = say it without comparing (plain numbers from allowed_numbers). The facts_text describes the data; it is not a phrase list. A question to the reader that names no company, sector or number is exempt ('Which move surprised you most?')
rules.plain_words: SUPERSEDED by rules.verbatim for every item with fact_phrases (no free-form factual sentence at all). Older items: ROUND 2 (HQ 2026-10-19): every sentence that is not a claim phrase uses only plain words: the item's cashtags, company / person names and sectors, its allowed numbers and dates, its window ('on Friday', 'in the week to Oct 16', 'last week' for a week item), 'the 500 largest US-listed stocks', and a closed list of plain words (reported, filed, bought, sold, moved, rose, fell, gained, lost, dropped, declined, up, down, closed, market value, earnings, revenue, EPS, consensus, open-market, Form 4, picks, link in bio, ...). Any other word - a synonym of best / only ('alone', 'just', 'the one', 'the rest', 'other', 'exception', 'took gold', 'star'), an order or table word, a streak word ('kept', 'continued', 'extended', 'another', 'deepened'), an equality word ('same', 'matched', 'equaled'), an intensity verb ('surged', 'tanked', 'sold off', 'in the green', 'higher', 'lower'), a number word ('three'), a month ('in October'), 'every' / 'all' / 'each', an arrow / medal emoji, or > < = - makes the sentence need to be a claim phrase verbatim. Numbers and moves are tied to their subject: each number goes right after the company / sector it belongs to ('$MSFT −1.13%', never '$MSFT +2.03%' when +2.03% is $AAPL's), and rose / fell / up / down must match the move of every company / sector it is said of (never a move the item does not give, never negated, never with will / could / may).
rules.claims: superseded by claim_phrases (kept for the direction / date reading): comparatives and superlatives (led, biggest, largest, worst, best, most, least, only, first, top, #1, record, 'outperformed every other') only as the item's claims state them: name only that claim's companies / sectors in that sentence; each claim has a polarity (best = top gainer, worst = top loser, null = no side) and a rank (1 = its one subject is #1; group = its subjects are the top N in order) and a metric (usd_change, pct_change, market_cap, ...): say the side with the noun ('top loser', 'led the drop', 'biggest gainer'; 'top' / 'led' / '#1' alone or with an entity noun ('top sector', 'led its sector') read as best, whatever number stands beside them; with any other noun ('led the rout', 'top casualty') say best / worst instead), say the metric as the claim does (dollars vs percent vs market cap), the singular ('the biggest drop') only for the rank-1 subject, a list only from #1 in order, 'among the biggest' for other members, 'the two biggest' / 'one of the two biggest' only for the top 2; '#N by <metric>' only as the item's rank_by_usd / rank_by_cap / claims state it; 'of the 500' / 'overall' / 'of all' / 'on the day' only with a claim that has no within, 'of the 10' for the basket; a sector only as a sector claim (kind sector) says, a stock 'within' a sector only with that sector next to the word ('in Tech', 'Tech's', 'its sector'); a company named in words (Microsoft) counts as its cashtag; a sentence that names no company ('It was the biggest...', 'The biggest dollar drop of the 500.') is about the one named before it; 'too' / 'so was X' after a superlative adds X to it; a question is checked like a statement (only one about the reader, naming nothing, is exempt); 'did better than' / 'outperformed' / 'fell more than' compare percent unless dollars are named, and need a claim of that metric; never widen the window ('ever', 'in months', 'of the quarter', 'since September', a week on a one-session item) or call the session 'today' / 'yesterday' / 'this morning' / 'pre-market' / another weekday unless the item's when does; no negated comparisons; never say a stock led its sector unless sector_leaders / claims say so; never put a company in a sector its ticker_sectors entry does not show
rules.moves: each item's moves: numbers = the sign of every number it allows with one sign, subjects = the direction of every company / sector it describes; never put a gain word (rose, gained, up) beside a loss or a loss word beside a gain ('Energy fell 2.6%' when Energy rose)

pillars.P0: picks + scoreboard (max 1 a day per platform)
pillars.P3: smart money in names you know (congress_flow, insider_flow, form4_buy, congress_trade, ptr_summary)
pillars.P7: breadth and the typical stock (breadth_day, basket_week)

variety: no same pillar twice in a row among a platform's own posts
at most 2 posts per pillar per platform per day
the same primary ticker on one platform not within 3 trading days (earnings results exempt)
a first line sharing >= 60% of its first 8 words with one of the platform's last 10 own posts is rejected
the same item on 2+ platforms: a different first line and >= 30% different wording
market-level pillars (P1 P2 P3 flows P4 P6 P7) >= 50% of own posts per platform per week; single filings <= 25%; picks <= 1 a day; <= 1 small-cap post in 4 (defaults; Growth tunes them)
the item's angles are first-line seeds, not templates: rotate the angle per pillar
rules.wording: every post of every item type: our universe is 'the 500 largest US-listed stocks' (or 'the 500 largest US-listed companies'), never 'S&P 500', 'S&P', 'SPX' or 'the index' (only a picks post may compare with the benchmark, as 'vs SPY'); 'the 10 largest US-listed companies', not 'US companies'; a 5-session window is worded as the item's when field says ('in the week to Oct 16', 'last week'); the 30-day insider totals are 'open-market buys / sells by officers and directors over 30 days in our feed'; a post never contradicts its card (card_message); market items: no 'crash', 'bloodbath', 'dump'
rules.cards: a market item's media is its pinned share card (card.url, a file on our Pages site, the same numbers the item states); never the live /market/card/ URL, never another day's card; no link in the main post: the UTM link goes in a self-reply

reasons.sector_rotation: day: best minus worst sector 2.4 pp < 3.0 pp; week: the session is not a Friday
reasons.basket_week: the session is not a Friday (the basket is a week-in-review item)
reasons.congress_flow: not due (weekly on Saturday / Monday, or when a 500-largest name enters the top 5)
